summary: Esho Yamaguchi (b. 1918) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1944) and held posts at Ritsumeikan University (~1952–1970) and Osaka University (~1970–1982).
Eshun Otsuka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University, where he also held a research student post attested in 2013.

Estela Piccin is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Unicamp, Associação Buddha-Dharma, Methodist University of São Paulo (PhD 2022), and Buddha-Dharma Centre of Hong Kong, later working at Prefeitura Municipal de Campinas.

Ester Bianchi (b. 1971) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert, and held appointments at Ca' Foscari, Florence, and Perugia (Associate Professor 2015).
Ethan Kroll is an Indology scholar who held posts at Baker McKenzie and on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies, both attested in 2012.
Etienne Vermeersch (1934–2019) was a Belgian philosopher. He studied at Ghent University (~1953–1965) and served on the faculty there from 1967 to 1997.
Etsuaki Teraishi is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts as an assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a JSPS special researcher (attested 2001).

Eugen Hultzsch (1857–1927) was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig and Bonn, and under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in India (1886–1903) and held the chair of Sanskrit at Halle-Wittenberg (1903–1925).

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied at Polytechnikum Riga and Riga Technical University, and served as a professor and language lecturer at Tongwen Guan (1881–1889).

Eugen Prym (1843–1913) specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig (under Heinrich Fleischer), and Bonn (under Johann Gildemeister), where he became Privatdozent of Oriental Languages in 1870.

Eugen Rose (1909–2003) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his education with studies at the University of Königsberg (1929), the University of Bonn (1929–1933), and the University of Marburg (1929–1941).

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Jena under August Schleicher and at Halle-Wittenberg, later serving as professor at Carolo-Alexandrinum and the University of Jena (from 1887).

Eugene N. Lane (1936–2007) was a scholar of history and archaeology. He was educated at Princeton University (~1954–1958) and Harvard University (~1958–1962), and held faculty posts at the University of Virginia (~1961–1966) and the University of Missouri (~1966–2000).

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Yale, Penn, Harvard under Charles Lanman, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, later lecturing in Pāli at Yale (1917–1932).

Eugene Y. Wang is a scholar of art history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. Educated under John M. Rosenfield and Hung Wu, he taught at the University of Chicago (~1996–1997) before becoming Professor of Asian Art at Harvard (~1997).
Eugeni d'Ors (1881–1954) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona (~1898–1905) and Universidad Central (~1905–1913), where he later held an academic post.

Eugenia Vanina (b. 1957) is a scholar of Indology and history. She studied at Moscow State University (1975–1981) and joined the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences as a researcher in 1985.

Eugenio Frola (1906–1962) was an Italian scholar active in Indology and mathematics. He studied engineering and mathematics at Turin and served as assistant and professor of mathematics at the Polytechnic University of Turin (~1930–1962).
Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck (1913–2003) was a Dutch linguist. He studied at Leiden University (~1932–1949) and subsequently served as a professor there from 1950 to 1983.

Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz (1901–1981) was a Polish Indologist and linguist. Educated at Jagiellonian and Lviv universities and in Paris, he held posts at Lviv (1922–1945), Nicolaus Copernicus University (1945–1953), and the University of Warsaw (1953–1971).
